fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream. Version 1.0, model name 'none', no Param and no Pairs. Schema-valid per the class test's isValid section.
Unmodified upstream. Model 'linear' with slope=3.141593 and intercept=2.718282 written at six significant digits, which is why the class test compares them with TEST_REAL_SIMILAR and not exactly.
Unmodified upstream. The deliberately invalid file: it carries a second </Transformation> close tag, so it is not well-formed XML at all, not merely schema-invalid.

source_anchors.operation: the constructor pins the handler version to 1.1 and the schema to /SCHEMAS/TrafoXML_1_1.xsd; this port exposes both as VERSION and SCHEMA_LOCATION
load always calls setDataPoints and only calls fitModel when fit_model is set, so the fit_model=false path returns a description whose model type has been reset to 'none' and whose model name is lost
store throws Exception::IllegalArgument 'will not write a transformation with empty name' for an empty model type
os.precision(writtenDigits<double>(0.0)) sets 15 significant digits, but Param values are written through ParamValue::toString() and only the Pair from/to attributes use the stream precision

a ParamValue::EMPTY_VALUE parameter is skipped; INT_VALUE writes type="int", DOUBLE_VALUE writes type="float", and STRING_VALUE together with all three list types writes type="string", so a list is flattened into its bracketed text and cannot be read back as a list
the default branch calls fatalError(STORE, ...) for any other value type
<Pairs> is written only when the data points are non-empty, with count equal to their number
the note attribute is written only when non-empty, and it is the only attribute passed through writeXMLEscape; from and to are not escaped because they are numbers
a file version above the parser's is only warned about, with the message 'This might lead to undefined program behavior'; this port refuses it
an unsupported <Param type> reaches error(LOAD, ...), which only logs, so the parameter is silently dropped; this port returns Error::Unsupported

<Pairs count> is only passed to data_.reserve and never compared with the number of <Pair> children, so a disagreement is accepted; this port accepts it too but checks the count against max_data_points first
an unknown element reaches warning(LOAD, ...), which logs at debug level in a release build and drops the element; this port returns Error::Unsupported
XMLHandler::error only writes to OPENMS_LOG_ERROR and returns; it does not throw, which is why an unsupported Param type is a silent loss
XMLHandler::warning writes to OPENMS_LOG_WARN only under OPENMS_ASSERTIONS and to OPENMS_LOG_DEBUG otherwise

fitModel returns immediately when the previous model type was 'identity', and throws Exception::IllegalArgument "unknown model type" for a name outside none/identity/linear/b_spline/lowess/interpolated
symmetric_regression is read into symmetric_ and then never used; the header documents a symmetric regression the implementation does not perform
an empty x/y_weight string means unweighted, for TrafoXML files written before OpenMS 3.0

evidence: Tier 3 source review. The expectations in tests/transformation_xml.rs are transcribed class-test literals from TransformationXMLFile_test.cpp: model names 'none'/'linear'/'interpolated', parameter counts 0/2/2, slope pi and intercept e compared with TEST_REAL_SIMILAR's relative tolerance, the three pairs (1.2,5.2) (2.2,6.25) (3.2,7.3), extrapolation_type 'two-point-linear' appearing in a reloaded interpolated model, the fit_model=false path reporting 'none', structural accept/reject outcomes on the four fixtures (a weaker substitute, not implementation of source XSD isValid), and Exception::IllegalArgument for the model name 'mumble_pfrwoarpfz'. Transcribed literals are tier-3 evidence: they detect transcription drift but cannot falsify a misread algorithm. No C++ was built or executed and no C++ output was retained, so nothing here is tier 1 or 2. The escaping round trip, the non-ASCII note, the coordinate-weight round trip, the version and unknown-element refusals and the resource ceilings are independently derived (tier 4) because no upstream fixture reaches them.
gaps: b_spline is a model TransformationDescription::fitModel accepts and src/analysis/transformations.rs does not implement, so a TrafoXML naming it reads as a record and returns Error::Unsupported when its model is resolved. The file's parameters and pairs are still readable through read_record_with_options.

Internal::XMLFile::isValid performs XSD validation against the bundled TrafoXML_1_1.xsd. This port has no XSD validator for TrafoXML (src/format/mzml_schema.rs is mzML-only and needs the libxml feature); the structural reader accepts three fixtures and rejects the malformed fourth. This does not implement or establish equivalent XSD validation.

The source's exact output bytes are not reproduced: attribute order within an element follows the shared XML writer (alphabetical) rather than the source's type/name/value, the source's two spaces after '<Param' are not emitted, and indentation is two spaces per level rather than a tab. Content, escaping and the round trip are equivalent; upstream compares trafoXML with FuzzyDiff, not byte-for-byte.

A data-fitted linear model in C++ carries the eight merged weight and datum defaults in its Param and writes all of them. This port writes slope, intercept and the weight parameters only when a weight is not the identity, so a file written here is smaller and independent of how the model was constructed. Both forms read back to the same model.

The source writes a list-valued parameter as type="string" holding its bracketed text, which cannot be read back as a list. This port reproduces that on writing and therefore inherits the same one-way conversion.
